verdicts.feasibility: Feasible with what exists, but it depends on C3 for the vertical half. Sound Analysis is not imported anywhere today. I checked it on this Mac (macOS 26.5.1): SNClassifySoundRequest(classifierIdentifier: .version1) reports 303 known classifications, including laughter, belly_laugh, baby_laughter, applause, clapping, cheering, gasp, screaming, speech and music. The non-verbal signal is real and on device. Ranking with Claude on the user's key fits the BYO-key rule and the existing Assistant lane. On-device FoundationModels is available on this Mac, but a session's context is 4,096 tokens (Apple TN3193). A one-hour transcript (~10k words) needs many chunk sessions and a second cross-chunk pass, and a ~3B model's judgement of 'the best moment' is the whole product, so treat it as a weak fallback. OpusClip, Riverside, Descript, Kapwing, Submagic and CapCut all ship it. verdicts.corrections: (a) Transcripts carry speaker labels only when an AssemblyAI transcript was requested with speakers:true. On-device transcripts have none. verdicts.closest_existing: Hand-made punch-ins: set_video's x, y and scale per clip, and add_zoom_action (the screencast zoom, core/src/edit_zoom.rs). Remove Silences and filler removal leave separate clips after ripple_delete_ranges, so each piece can take its own scale with no action. Speed below ×1 shows the nearest source frame on every output frame, with no blending or interpolation; ramps are per-canvas-frame segments (speed_segments.rs). Transitions are the TransitionKind enum in core/src/model.rs (13 kinds, no 'smooth'). The ReverseRenderer/ReverseCache/BackgroundRender pattern writes a derived per-media file.
verdicts.feasibility: Punch-in is an easy fit. It is a pure core rule over cuts within one media's continuous take, writing set_video x, y and scale, with the face centre from C3's Vision analysis or a plain centre fallback. ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit (ProjectDocument.swift:1121) already makes several ops one undo step for the menu command. The interpolation half is harder. I checked on this Mac (macOS 26.5.1): VTFrameRateConversionConfiguration and VTMotionBlurConfiguration both report isSupported true, an 8192×4320 configuration initialises, and supportedPixelFormats is ONLY 'RGhA' (REDACTED) for both. So 10-bit input is not a bit-depth problem, and the format matches the 16-bit-float compositor. But every source needs a half-float conversion (~66 MB per 4K frame), and whether HLG/PQ-encoded or extended-range values interpolate correctly is still untested. The 'smooth' kind does not fit the model: a transition IS an overlap of two clips (transition.rs), so no transition exists 'at an abutting cut'. A smooth cut would have to be an overlap built from handles by add_transition's handle form (the removed filler supplies the handles), with a rendered morph in place of the dissolve, or a short derived clip. VT frame-rate conversion synthesises frames between CONSECUTIVE frames, and bridging a jump cut with a pose change is Morph Cut territory where artefacts are likely. Spike it before promising it. Slow-motion interpolation is the use Apple names (WWDC25 session 300: 'Interpolate 3 frames between reference frames for 4x slow-mo'). Spec §1 lists motion blur and optical-flow retiming as non-goals, so a §11 decision lifts them first.
verdicts.platform_apis: VideoToolbox VTFrameProcessor (macOS 15.4+): VTFrameRateConversionConfiguration/Parameters (interpolation phases, optional precomputed VTOpticalFlowConfiguration) and VTMotionBlurConfiguration/Parameters (strength 1–100). Both support up to 8192×4320 on macOS, and both take only 64RGBAHalf on this Mac. Vision face rectangles (10.13+) for the punch-in centre. The existing BackgroundRender, ReverseCache and MediaCacheLedger.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: I tried to show creators don't need it, or that it is commoditised or distrusted. Punch-in survives. It is the standard YouTuber fix for jump cuts: Riverside's own October 2026 tutorial teaches turning a jump cut into a zoom cut, and Gling ships auto zoom. It is cheap, exact and needs no disclosure. Generated smooth cuts are weaker. Descript's 'Smooth jump cuts' / Smooth all exists, runs on Regenerate (generative AI) and spends AI credits; I found no per-second rate. I found NO Riverside 'Smooth cuts' feature. Optical-flow morphs across cuts are historically unreliable (Premiere Morph Cut), and VT frame-rate conversion was not built for that. Optical-flow slow motion is valued for B-roll but is a pro-editor feature, and many creators shoot 60/120 fps on phones. YouTube's disclosure policy exempts minor edits, special effects and production assistance, so interpolation is not a disclosure risk. Net: punch-in holds strongly, slow motion moderately, smooth cuts via VT do not hold until a spike.
verdicts.corrections: (a) Scale and position are set_video's (x, y, scale). set_clip only sets a clip's name and label. (b) Transition kinds are the TransitionKind enum in core/src/model.rs, set by set_transition. set_transition_style changes only easing and audio and leaves the kind alone. A transition is an OVERLAP, so a kind 'valid only at an abutting cut' contradicts the model. (c) VTFrameProcessor accepts only 64RGBAHalf here (checked on macOS 26.5.1). The 10-bit question becomes a conversion-cost and HDR-encoding question. (d) Descript's feature runs on Regenerate (generative), not optical flow, and bills AI credits; per-second billing is unverified. (e) No Riverside 'Smooth cuts' feature was found. Riverside teaches manual zoom cuts instead. (f) YouTube's disclosure rules exempt special effects and production assistance, so interpolation is not a disclosure issue. (g) Split it. Punch-in is S and should ship alone. Slow motion is M after a spike. VT smooth cuts stay a spike, not a commitment.

verdicts.closest_existing: Every Assistant or MCP tool call is its own undo step, by spec §11 AI-10 ('Risk accepted: a ten-call turn is ten Undos'; docs/guide/assistant.md:117). ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit (ProjectDocument.swift:1121, AgentServer.swift:616) already folds several ops into one named undo step. The Export Queue already pins and renders a ReelProject other than the window's current one (ExportQueueController.swift pinnedProject). CompositionBuilder.build takes a plan, not the document. There is no project diff export. mcp-proxy answers initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call only, with capabilities {tools:{listChanged:true}}, and core/src/agent.rs advertises {tools:{}}. AssistantPrompt.swift has no recipes. agent/src/pricing.ts price(usage, model, table) prices usage after it happens.
verdicts.feasibility: Proposals fit the architecture well. Handles are immutable, every edit is a pure op answering applied, identity or refused in the rule's own sentence, a non-current project already renders (the export pin), and performGroupedEdit already gives a one-step accept. New pieces: an rc_project_diff export (Rust, header, ReelCore.swift lockstep), a proposal envelope key beside scope (scope.rs's exhaustive refused_inside shows the pattern), open/accept/discard tools with catalog and parity rows, and timeline ghost and strike drawing. It amends spec §11 AI-10, which explicitly accepted ungrouped turns, so a new §11 decision must come before the code. Recipes as data fit R5-1 (closed vocabularies, never a runtime) and G-1, because the LLM interprets them and Frame Job executes nothing. But shareable .fjrecipe files are a prompt-injection surface: a shared recipe's brief can steer the agent to export, delete or overwrite. Each recipe's allowed-tool list must be enforced by the gate and checked against AssistantToolTable's withheld and ask-first rows. Serving recipes as MCP prompts needs prompts/list and prompts/get in mcp-proxy. core/src/agent.rs is generic code copied from Rasterize ('do not add domain knowledge'), so the in-socket server would need a generic prompt hook or would not serve them. A cost 'up front' can only be an estimate range from past runs: pricing.ts prices a usage object, and an agentic run's tokens are unknown in advance.
verdicts.platform_apis: No Apple API. The core FFI (a new rc_project_diff), the existing undo grouping (performGroupedEdit), the composition plan and recipe from any handle, the MCP prompts capability (prompts/list, prompts/get) in mcp-proxy, and agent/src/pricing.ts with the LiteLLM table for an estimate range.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: I tried to show creators don't care about agent trust, or that it is commoditised. Adobe's 2026 Creators' Toolkit Report (Harris Poll, 16,000+ creators in 8 countries, May 2026) supports the need. Among creators who want more agent independence, 44% prioritise being able to review, edit or undo, and 37% want visibility into what the agent does. Regional figures differ (Australia 46%/38%, India 54%/42%), and 85% say the final decision must stay with the creator. The weak form is already commoditised: Kapwing shows an editable plan, Descript Underlord has review and Revert, Riverside asks for sign-off. Playing the whole proposed cut before accepting it, with A/B against the current cut, is distinctive and only cheap here because of immutable handles. Against it: this is a second-order feature that matters only once creators actually use the agent, and agent use on a BYO Anthropic key is itself limited by cost. Recipes are the creator-visible half, but their headline example ('Podcast episode → 6 vertical clips') needs C3 and C6 first. I could not verify the market claims about official MCP servers (Descript, Kapwing, Riverside, 'Resolve 21.1', Apple's iWork): the Resolve and FCP MCP servers I found are community projects, and Resolve's need Studio for external scripting. The case survives narrowly as a differentiator and enabler, not as a headline.
verdicts.corrections: (a) N-edit turns giving N undo steps is a recorded spec §11 decision (AI-10, risk accepted), not merely a documented limit, so Proposals must record an amending decision first. (b) One-step grouping already exists (performGroupedEdit), so 'accept as one step' is cheap and the new work is the diff, the side chain and the diff view. (c) pricing.ts cannot price a run before it starts. It prices a usage object, so 'estimated cost first' must be an estimate range. (d) core/src/agent.rs is generic Rasterize code with tools-only capabilities, so prompts belong in mcp-proxy or need a generic hook. (e) Shareable .fjrecipe files add a prompt-injection path that needs gate-enforced tool allow-lists. (f) The official MCP-server claims (Descript, Kapwing, Riverside, Resolve 21.1, Apple iWork) are unverified: the Resolve and FCP servers found are community-built, and Resolve's require Studio. (g) The Adobe 44%/37% figures are the global numbers among creators wanting more agent independence, and regional figures differ. (h) Effort is M for Proposals and M for Recipes, L together. Recipes' best demos depend on C3 and C6.

verdicts.closest_existing: Manual reframing only. set_canvas changes the size and, when rescale_clips is true, moves every clip's x, y and scale by the size ratio, with scale following the SMALLER ratio (a Fit), never a Fill (core/src/edit_canvas.rs rescale). Project::fill_scale (core/src/edit_fit.rs) is used only by add_background and add_blurred_background (core/src/edit_background.rs, Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background). Word captions size to the canvas's shorter side (app/Sources/CaptionStyle.swift:146; docs/guide/captions.md:164). Graphic modules receive ctx.canvas, the PROJECT's size even inside a nest (core/src/recipe_graphic.rs:93-138). add_zoom_action is the hand-placed screencast zoom. No subject analysis and no tracking.
verdicts.feasibility: Feasible as offline analysis that writes ordinary x, y and scale actions, so the one-pass compositor stays as it is. Four things are harder than the candidate says. (1) Vision is not imported anywhere in app/Sources. The only Vision code is the iceboxed E9 spike in tools/proof/effects_spike/vision_*.swift (#124). That spike found VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest flickers on video (up to 57% of pixels flip between masks 0.1 s apart), so the planner should take face, human and saliency rectangles plus VNTrackObjectRequest, not masks. (2) MediaImporter.CacheLane is a width-2 lane for AUDIO decodes, and thumbnails are deliberately kept off it, so per-media video analysis needs its own lane, cache kind and ledger rows. (3) Two actions on one clip may not overlap AT ALL, whatever they animate (edit_action.rs overlapping_action). So any clip that already has an action (a zoom, a volume or grade action, a speed ramp) needs a wrapping nest, and a nest's canvas is frozen at its size when nested. (4) set_canvas does not rescale action end patches (edit_canvas.rs), so existing zoom actions on a screencast keep their 16:9 targets after the change, and the planner must rewrite or replace them. The cursor path from C2 does not exist: nothing records the cursor today. Linked versions (several canvases in one project, per-clip framing overrides keyed by clip id) are a schema change with a format bump, against a model that has exactly one canvas. Spec §1 names auto-reframe a non-goal because of 'heavy pixel work or ML, outside the compositor's one-pass shape'. Analysis-into-actions removes that reason, but a §11 decision must lift it first.
